lessons.title: Why Hands-On Practice Matters in Salesforce

slots.practicalActivity: Before creating anything, write down in your own words why Salesforce certification exams and the real job are scenario-based rather than definition-based, and list the three things this chapter will set up for you (a Trailhead account, a Trailhead Playground, and a clear understanding of how a Playground, a Developer Edition org, and a sandbox differ). Open trailhead.salesforce.com in a browser tab to confirm it's reachable.
slots.deliverable: A short written note naming the chapter's three deliverables and one sentence on why repetition in Setup beats reading about it.

slots.practicalActivity: Go to trailhead.salesforce.com, click Sign Up, and create a real Trailblazer account using an email address you'll still have access to in a year — not a Salesforce trial org login. Once in, open your Settings page (Privacy, Connected Accounts, Email Preferences) from your profile icon and note the default Profile Privacy setting.
slots.deliverable: A working Trailblazer login (note the username, never the password), plus a one-line note on the account's current Profile Privacy setting.

slots.practicalActivity: From your Hands-On Orgs page (trailhead.salesforce.com/me/hands-on-orgs), click Create Playground, name it something recognizable like 'LTV Training Org' instead of the random default, and wait for it to finish provisioning (typically 3-4 minutes). Once it's ready, click Launch to confirm you can log straight into Setup.
slots.deliverable: One newly created, clearly named Trailhead Playground that successfully launches into Setup.

slots.practicalActivity: In your new playground, go to Setup -> Company Information and confirm the Organization Edition field reads 'Developer Edition'. Note, in your own words, the two concrete limits that cap it: two paid user licenses and roughly 10MB of data storage.
slots.deliverable: A screenshot or written note of the Organization Edition value plus the two stated Developer Edition limits.

lessons.title: Trailhead Playground vs. Developer Edition vs. Sandbox

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short three-row comparison table distinguishing a Trailhead Playground, a standalone Developer Edition org, and a sandbox, focused specifically on the one distinction that actually matters: where each one's data comes from (empty and personal, vs. a copy of a real company's production data).
slots.deliverable: A three-row written comparison table (Playground / Developer Edition org / Sandbox) centered on the data-origin distinction.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the playground you created this chapter, write a one-paragraph 'org passport' combining everything from this chapter: your Trailblazer username, your playground's name, its confirmed Developer Edition status and two limits, and a one-sentence explanation of why this specific org (not a trial, not a sandbox) is the one you'll use across the rest of this career path.
slots.deliverable: One written 'org passport' paragraph tying together real, specific details from your own Trailhead account and playground.

slots.practicalActivity: In your playground, click the gear icon to open Setup, then deliberately click the grid (App Launcher) icon right next to it to confirm you can tell the two apart. Browse the Setup sidebar and find one item under Administration and one under Platform Tools, then open Object Manager from its own top-level tab next to Home.
slots.deliverable: A short written note naming one Administration sidebar item, one Platform Tools sidebar item, and confirming you opened Object Manager from its dedicated tab.

lessons.title: Using Setup Search and Quick Find

slots.practicalActivity: Practice all three search patterns from the lesson: type a Setup page name into Search Setup at the top of the page, use the sidebar's Quick Find to filter the left-hand category list, then open Object Manager on any object and use its own Quick Find to filter the Fields & Relationships list down to one field.
slots.deliverable: A written note of the specific term you searched in each of the three search boxes and exactly what each one returned.

slots.practicalActivity: Click your profile photo and open Settings. Under Personal Information, confirm your name, email, and time zone. Go to Language & Time Zone and deliberately change your time zone to a different one to see a record's displayed date/time shift, then change it back.
slots.deliverable: A before/after note of the time zone you set and the specific date/time field whose displayed value you watched change.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup, search 'Company Information' in Quick Find. Record your org's Organization ID and Instance. Scroll to the User Licenses table and note Total, Used, and Remaining for the 'Salesforce' license type, then check the Data Storage table for which record type (Contacts, Opportunities, etc.) is currently using the most storage.
slots.deliverable: The org's Organization ID and Instance, the Salesforce license Remaining count, and the top storage-consuming record type.

lessons.title: Sample Data and Resetting Your Org

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Accounts tab in your playground and find the pre-loaded sample record (such as 'Acme') clearly marked '(Sample)' in its name. Visit the Sample Gallery at developer.salesforce.com and note one full sample app available there, such as Coral Cloud Resorts or LWC Recipes.
slots.deliverable: The name of one real pre-loaded sample record found in your org, plus one named Sample Gallery app and what it demonstrates.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page 'Setup survival sheet' for your future self combining this chapter: the exact rule for choosing Search Setup vs. the sidebar's Quick Find vs. Object Manager's own Quick Find, where personal Settings and admin Setup diverge, and what Company Information's three categories of information are (identity, edition/instance, licenses/storage).
slots.deliverable: One written reference sheet covering the search-box rule, the Settings-vs-Setup distinction, and Company Information's three categories.

slots.practicalActivity: Go back to your Hands-On Orgs page and confirm your playground's name is recognizable, renaming it if it's still the random default. Open Setup's 'Install a Package' tool and note that it asks whether to install into 'Production' or a 'Sandbox' (Production is your only real option, since a personal playground has no sandbox underneath it). Set a recurring monthly calendar reminder to log in and keep the org active.
slots.deliverable: A confirmed, clearly-named playground, a note on what 'Install a Package' asked when opened, and confirmation of the recurring login reminder you set.

lessons.title: Organizing Your Work: Naming and Notes

slots.practicalActivity: Create one test Account and one test Contact in your playground using a consistent, course-prefixed, dated naming convention (e.g. 'SF-Admin-Test Account 2026-10'). Open the Notes tool from the App Launcher's All Items list and attach a short note to one of them explaining what it's for and when it's safe to delete.
slots.deliverable: One course-prefixed, dated test record plus one attached Note explaining its purpose and deletion timing.

lessons.title: Using Trailhead Modules and Superbadges With LTV

slots.practicalActivity: Open your Trailblazer profile (reachable from your Trailhead account) and note what it currently shows. Start one real, free Trailhead module relevant to Salesforce administration and complete its first hands-on challenge, letting Trailhead verify it automatically against your connected playground.
slots.deliverable: One completed Trailhead module unit, auto-verified against your own playground, plus a screenshot of the resulting badge or points on your Trailblazer profile.

lessons.title: Getting Help: Documentation and the Trailblazer Community

slots.practicalActivity: Click the question-mark Help icon on any Setup page in your playground and read one contextual help article for that page. Search help.salesforce.com directly for a real 'how do I' question you still have from this course. Browse the Trailblazer Community Groups directory and join one group relevant to Salesforce administration.
slots.deliverable: The help article title you read, the real question you searched on help.salesforce.com with what you found, and the name of the Trailblazer Community Group you joined.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the same playground, naming convention, and Notes habit from this chapter, create a small 'practice project': two Accounts, two Contacts tied to them, and one Note on each explaining what course or lesson it's for — following the naming and documentation habits from this chapter — then look up one open question about your work in the Trailblazer Community.
slots.deliverable: Two Accounts and two Contacts built with consistent, course-prefixed, dated names, each with an explanatory Note, plus one real Trailblazer Community search for an open question.

slots.practicalActivity: Course-closing lab: without re-reading the lessons, start from your Hands-On Orgs page and demonstrate, in one sitting, that your permanent org setup actually works. Launch your playground, confirm its Developer Edition status in Company Information, create one more properly named, dated, and noted test record, and look up one unfamiliar Setup term using Quick Find.
slots.deliverable: One completed end-to-end checklist run (launch, verify edition, create a named/dated/noted record, resolve one Setup lookup) with brief notes on each step.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student has their own permanent, named Trailhead Playground running on Developer Edition, knows exactly how to find anything in Setup, and has the account, naming, and help-seeking habits needed to use that same org across every remaining course in the Salesforce Administrator path.
